technical.lead: OpenAI buys Ona to give Codex agents persistent cloud sandboxes
technical.body: OpenAI announced on June 11 it is acquiring Ona - the German startup formerly known as Gitpod - for undisclosed terms pending regulatory approval, folding the team into the Codex group, per [SiliconANGLE - OpenAI acquires AI agent orchestration startup Ona](https://siliconangle.com/2026/06/11/openai-acquires-ai-agent-orchestration-startup-ona/). Ona runs coding agents inside persistent cloud sandboxes rather than on a developer's laptop, so a multi-hour or multi-day task keeps executing after the workstation powers off and the developer reviews it later; OpenAI frames the deal as letting Codex - now past 5 million weekly users - carry long-running software work to completion, per [The Tech Portal - OpenAI agrees to acquire AI cloud startup 'Ona', team will join Codex division](https://thetechportal.com/2026/06/11/openai-agrees-to-acquire-ai-cloud-startup-ona-team-will-join-codex-division/). European trade coverage reads it as OpenAI buying the durable-execution substrate Anthropic dominates inside enterprises, contesting the coding-agent fight one layer down - from raw model capability toward who owns the restart-surviving runtime - per [Techzine - As Anthropic claims the enterprise, OpenAI fights back with Ona deal](https://www.techzine.eu/news/devops/142087/as-anthropic-claims-the-enterprise-openai-fights-back-with-ona-deal/).

technical.lead: Zyphra open-sources Zamba2-VL, fast Mamba2-Transformer hybrid VLMs
technical.body: On June 12 Zyphra released Zamba2-VL, a family of open vision-language models at 1.2B, 2.7B, and 7B parameters under Apache 2.0, with checkpoints on Hugging Face and inference code in a custom transformers fork, per [MarkTechPost - Zyphra releases Zamba2-VL hybrid Mamba2-Transformer vision-language models](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/06/12/zyphra-release-zamba2-vl-hybrid-mamba2-transformer-vision-language-models-that-cut-time-to-first-token-by-about-an-order-of-magnitude/). The language backbone pairs Mamba2 state-space layers with a few shared transformer blocks and reuses the Qwen2.5-VL Vision Transformer through a two-layer MLP adapter, delivering roughly an order-of-magnitude lower time-to-first-token versus comparable transformer VLMs on 32K-token prefill - the latency regime that matters for on-device document and screen understanding. The small models are strong on perception: the 2.7B posts PixMoCount 82.5, CountBenchQA 87.5, and DocVQA 90.9, while the 1.2B reaches PixMoCount 62.5, nearly double the transformer-based InternVL3.5-1B at 32.8, per [Zyphra - Zamba2-VL](https://www.zyphra.com/our-work/zamba2-vl). It is a concrete open-weight data point that the SSM-hybrid backbone can carry multimodal perception at the 1-7B sizes that fit on local hardware.

citations.label: MarkTechPost - Zyphra releases Zamba2-VL hybrid Mamba2-Transformer vision-language models

technical.lead: Moonshot ships Kimi Work, a local 300-sub-agent swarm on Kimi K2.6
technical.body: Moonshot AI launched Kimi Work on June 12, a downloadable desktop app for Apple silicon and Windows rather than a web chat: the user states goals in plain language and the agent acts directly on the machine, coordinating an Agent Swarm that scales to about 300 sub-agents in parallel, driving the user's logged-in browser through a WebBridge extension and firing scheduled jobs via a built-in cron engine with a keep-awake toggle for overnight runs, per [MarkTechPost - Moonshot AI launches Kimi Work, a local desktop agent on Kimi K2.6 with a 300-sub-agent swarm](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/06/12/moonshot-ai-launches-kimi-work-a-local-desktop-agent-reportedly-running-on-kimi-k2-6-with-a-300-sub-agent-agent-swarm/). It reads mounted local folders and runs Python in the background, leaving original files untouched unless changes are approved. The engine is Kimi K2.6, an open-weight Mixture-of-Experts model with about 32B active parameters per token and 256K context, and the local-execution story is reinforced because the same weights already run on-device through Unsloth, whose Dynamic 2.0 quantization ships a 2-bit (UD-Q2_K_XL) build alongside near-lossless variants, per [Unsloth - Kimi K2.6: How to run locally](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/kimi-k2.6). The day's agent-layer signal is a fork: persistent off-machine sandboxes on one side, an always-on local swarm on the user's own files on the other.

technical.lead: AI-lab IPO race firms up as SpaceX prices the largest IPO ever
technical.body: The frontier-lab path to public markets firmed up this week. Anthropic confidentially filed a draft Form S-1 with the SEC on June 1 - on the back of the $65B round that set its $965B post-money valuation and a revenue run-rate past $47B, more than tripled since February - setting up an IPO season against OpenAI, which is targeting a raise of at least $60B at a valuation of up to $1 trillion and is expected to list by year's end, per [SiliconANGLE - Anthropic confidentially files for IPO amid rapid growth](https://siliconangle.com/2026/06/01/anthropic-confidentially-files-ipo-amid-rapid-growth/). The backdrop turned concrete on June 11 when SpaceX priced 555.6 million shares at $135 to raise about $75B - the largest IPO in history, eclipsing Saudi Aramco's 2019 debut, set to trade on Nasdaq under SPCX - resetting the ceiling for how much capital public markets will absorb for one high-multiple name, per [ZeroHedge - SpaceX Prices Biggest Ever IPO At $135 Per Share](https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/spacex-prices-biggest-ever-ipo-135-share). On distribution, OpenAI and Oracle moved to let Oracle Cloud customers apply eligible Universal Credits toward OpenAI's frontier models and Codex, routing AI workloads without a new procurement path, per [StartupHub.ai - OpenAI teams up with Oracle Cloud](https://www.startuphub.ai/ai-news/artificial-intelligence/2026/openai-teams-up-with-oracle-cloud).

technical.lead: Summer AI-event calendar firms up: Databricks Summit opens Monday
technical.body: With Apple's WWDC26 reaching its final day today, the still-upcoming AI calendar worth planning attendance around continues across three tracks. On the mainstream developer and data side, the Databricks Data + AI Summit opens June 15-18 across Moscone North, West and South (30,000-plus in person, 800-plus sessions, keynotes from Databricks' co-founders plus OpenAI's Greg Brockman and a recorded Satya Nadella fireside), per [San Francisco Tribune - Databricks brings Data + AI Summit back to San Francisco](https://thesanfranciscotribune.com/databricks-brings-data-ai-summit-back-to-san-francisco-as-enterprise-ai-event-calendar-grows/), and the AI Engineer World's Fair runs June 29-July 2 at Moscone West with 29 tracks including dedicated Inference and Security tracks, per [AI Red Team - AI Engineer World's Fair 2026](https://www.ai-redteam.com/insights/worldsfair26/). On the security track, the Confidential Computing Summit lands June 23-24 at the San Francisco Mint, SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit follows August 11-12, and Black Hat USA's AI Summit (August 4) plus DEF CON's AI Village anchor the agentic red-teaming calendar. On the chip track, AMD's Advancing AI 2026 is locked to July 22-23 at Moscone (MI400-series availability expected, MI450 unveil anticipated), Hot Chips 2026 takes Stanford August 23-25, and the AI Infra Summit runs September 15-17 at Santa Clara.
